suppress.notes: Justification: CVE-2026-53914 (NVD/JetBrains advisory) is unsafe deserialization in the Kotlin Gradle build cache's metadata handling — a build-time/compiler-tooling vulnerability, fixed in the Kotlin build tooling at 2.4.20. kotlin-stdlib / kotlin-stdlib-common are runtime jars pulled in transitively by okhttp (see pom.xml, direct okhttp dependency) purely as a runtime classpath dependency; this project is Java/Maven, never invokes the Kotlin compiler or a Gradle build cache, so the vulnerable code path (build-cache metadata deserialization) has no reachable attack surface here. Confirmed false-positive CPE match against the Kotlin product line as a whole, not the runtime stdlib artifact. No fixed *stable* kotlin-stdlib release exists yet (2.4.20 line is still pre-release as of this triage); revisit once one ships, or if kotlin-stdlib ever becomes more than a transitive runtime dependency here.

Justification: CVE-2026-41717 (Spring Data MongoDB SpEL expression-injection in @Query capture-all placeholder binding) affects the spring-data-mongodb artifact versions 5.0.0-5.0.5, fixed in 5.0.6 per the vendor advisory (spring.io/security/cve-2026-41717). This project's actual spring-data-mongodb runtime version is 5.0.6 (confirmed via `mvnw dependency:tree`) — already the fixed release. The finding is a CPE mismatch: dependency-check flagged spring-boot-data-mongodb-4.0.7.jar, which is Spring Boot's own autoconfig wrapper module (versioned along Spring Boot's release train, currently 4.0.7) — a different artifact from spring-data-mongodb that happens to get matched against the same CPE. Confirmed false positive; the real vulnerable library is already on the patched version.
